method: A pre-document MutationObserver recorded the first visible enabled composer.
Chrome DevTools Protocol navigation timing, Network, Performance and V8 tracing measured the exact Edge browser.
Cold runs cleared the browser cache before navigation; warm runs reloaded the same fresh profile without clearing cache.
No model request, account switch, service restart or repository mutation was performed by the measurement.

decision.primary_next_step: reduce initial JavaScript parse and initialization work using upstream-compatible source/chunk boundaries
decision.secondary_next_step: prefer the existing Brotli sibling over gzip when encoding quality is equal

tests.result: 3 cold and 3 warm authenticated 8216 document loads returned HTTP 200 and rendered the composer
blocked after a bounded 30-second session timeout; no Safari performance result claimed

residual_risks: Safari cold and warm timing remains unqualified until macOS Safari automation authorization is functional.
Three observations per state are a decision baseline, not a soak test or a stable speed guarantee.
The warm composer median shows that caching alone does not remove the multi-second renderer initialization cost.
